title: dep-lighthouse: add dependency-audit CLI and split lint executor for faster feedback
author: Maya Ortiz
release_notes: Add 'dep-lighthouse' CLI for dependency freshness auditing and a split lint executor to reduce presubmit latency. No behavioral API changes. Backwards-compatible CI hooks; opt-in automation for auto-PRs.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial CLI scaffolding; lockfile parsers and heuristics; presubmit hook integration; split lint executor pipeline; tests + docs; followed by small fixes after reviewer feedback (typo, cache path).
description:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit feedback loop has trended upward as the monorepo grows: lint runs are taking longer and dependency churn causes noisy failure modes. This PR ships two coordinated changes: 1) a small CLI 'dep-lighthouse' that scans supported lockfiles (package-lock.json / poetry.lock / go.sum) to surface 'stale' transitive dependencies and optionally draft minimal bump PRs; 2) a refactor of the CI lint runner by splitting the monolithic lint job into language-specific executors to enable fast feedback for changed areas and to reduce noisy re-runs across unrelated languages.

What this PR does (single-continuous description): Adds a new lightweight Python CLI at tools/dep-lighthouse which implements lockfile parsing, a pluggable rule engine (age, resolution downgrade, advisory cross-check), and a presubmit mode that returns non-zero when a critical-staleness threshold is hit. The CLI can run in two modes: audit-only (outputs JSON/summary) and auto-pr (opens a draft branch with minimal package bump suggestions; auto-PR is behind a feature flag and requires token). CI changes: ci/presubmit-hooks/deps-audit.yml wires the audit as an optional presubmit that emits annotations and an artifact; the audit is gated to run only when lockfiles are touched to keep CI costs low. Lint refactor: ci/lint/executor-splitter.yml introduces three lightweight executors (js-ts, python, go) and a coordinator step that maps files changed to the minimal executor set. This pulls cache priming into a separate job (ci/actions/cache-primer.sh) to reduce repeated installs in parallel shards. Docs and developer UX: docs/dev/dep-lighthouse.md documents usage, thresholds, and how to opt-in the auto-pr flow.

Checklists: - [x] Unit tests for lockfile parsers and heuristics (tools/dep-lighthouse/tests) - [x] Integration test for presubmit hook (ci/test-presubmit.sh) - [x] Updated dev docs and quickstart - [x] CI matrix trimmed to run auditors only on lockfile changes - [x] Feature flag for auto-PR flows

Testing and CI: On first push, one lint shard failed due to path assumptions in the cache-primer script; fixed in commit 3 to use repository-root-aware paths. Final CI: full suite green (lint shards, unit tests, minimal integration smoke). See CI log: audit job (ran only once because no lockfile changes on one of the test pushes), js-ts lint (fast), python lint (isolated), go vet (unchanged).

Review notes and rationale: Splitting the lint executor reduces average presubmit wall time for focused changes by ~40% in local perf runs. The cache-primer separates expensive OS-level cache warm-up from per-shard installs; this reduces duplicated work when three shards run concurrently. Dep-lighthouse is intentionally conservative: it only suggests minimal patch updates and does not run automatic major upgrades. The feature-flagged auto-PR flow is opt-in and will be run by the maintainers team initially to validate signal quality.

High-level risk and mitigation: The presubmit hook returns non-zero only when the staleness heuristic crosses a threshold (configurable). For safety the default is audit-only; maintainers can enable auto-PR for a repository via repo settings. Lint behavior is unchanged aside from shard routing; no new formatter rules are added.

Files changed (high level): tools/dep-lighthouse/cli.py - main CLI and heuristics; tools/dep-lighthouse/parsers.py - lockfile parsers; tools/dep-lighthouse/tests/* - unit tests; ci/lint/executor-splitter.yml - pipeline split and coordinator mapping; ci/presubmit-hooks/deps-audit.yml - presubmit wiring; ci/actions/cache-primer.sh - separate cache warmup script; docs/dev/dep-lighthouse.md - developer guide.

Review conversation (summary): Kunal: "Nice isolation of the cache primer — can we make the primer idempotent across runners?" Reply (Maya): "Yes, updated script to be safe for concurrent runs and added a small file-lock on /tmp/dep-lighthouse-cache.lock; documented in the script and tests." Priya: "The staleness heuristic looks aggressive for some transitive deps, can we tune?" Reply: "Moved thresholds to repo config (docs updated) and reduced default sensitivity for transitive-only proposals; kept strictness for direct deps." Liam: "Suggest adding a small flag for maintainers to suppress auto-PRs for certain paths." Reply: "Added --suppress-paths to the CLI and wired to repo config; also added helpful errors in the docs." 

Merge outcome: After reviewer approvals and CI green, this was merged to main via squash. Follow-ups: ENG-4621 roadmap item to add GitHub-native annotations with quick-fix links (tracked), ENG-4780 to iterate on auto-PR heuristics.

Notes for on-call / SRE: If presubmit audits begin failing unexpectedly, the gating can be toggled off by removing the hook file or setting the environment variable DEPLIGHTHOUSE_MODE=audit in the presubmit entry. The CLI logs to stderr and emits a compressed JSON artifact when run in CI; the artifact key pattern is dep-lighthouse-audit-${{GITHUB_RUN_ID}}.
review_thread:
Kunal Shah: idempotency concern on cache-primer; Maya: implemented file-lock and added tests.
Priya Nair: reduce sensitivity on transitive deps; Maya: added repo-configurable thresholds and updated docs.
Liam O'Connor: opt-out flags for certain paths; Maya: added --suppress-paths and config.
All reviewers: approved after minor fixes.
notes: Visible perf wins in dev perf harness; will monitor presubmit latency and noise for 2 weeks post-merge.
manual_steps_for_ops:
(1) To disable audit presubmit: rm ci/presubmit-hooks/deps-audit.yml or set DEPLIGHTHOUSE_MODE=disabled in CI. (2) To run locally: python tools/dep-lighthouse/cli.py audit --path .
(3) To enable auto-PRs: set DEPLIGHTHOUSE_AUTO=true and provide GITHUB_TOKEN with push rights.
estimated_impact: Presubmit median feedback latency reduced ~40% for single-language changes in local benchmarks; CI cost neutral because audit only runs on lockfile changes by default.
